text:
- [LFAC.2.5.3] **The complement: a meaningful change
  is a replace, never a second fact, and is never
  silent.** A reassertion that is *not* a no-op under
  [LFAC.2.5.1] — a `tolerance`-bearing slot whose value
  moves outside the tolerance, or any exactly-compared
  slot that changes — is a **meaningful change**. The
  engine must apply it as a retract-and-replace per
  [LFAC.1.2.2]: the prior fact for that identity key
  ([LFAC.1.7]) is retracted and the new one asserted, so
  **exactly one live fact per key remains** (the live
  count is unchanged), the new fact is a fresh wrapper
  with a new `fact_id` ([IDAT.4.4]), and `ts` advances.
  The engine must surface this on the stream as
  `FACT_ASSERT(new)` followed by `FACT_RETRACT(old)`,
  whether a host assert or a rule's emit produced the
  new fact: the successor is recorded before the
  withdrawal it causes ([RFCS.6.7], [RFCS.6a.4]). `FACT_MODIFY` is reserved and not
  emitted ([NCBK.2.4]). An
  in-place same-wrapper mutation that emits no stream
  event, and any path that leaves a second live fact for
  the same key, are both non-conforming.

idris.name: lfac_2_5_3__churn_diverges
idris.note: Executed and checked: period 2 from the start. Each replace is a new fact, hence a new token, hence a firing -- the clause's retract-and-replace is a fresh production, and a rule that replaces what it matches never quiesces.

idris.name: lfac_2_5_3__churn
idris.note: `C c where c.key == 1 -> emit C key: 1 pay: flip(c.pay)`: every firing is a meaningful change of the same identity.

idris.name: lfac_2_5_3__churn_prog
idris.note: That rule alone, with C an entity (one-slot key) kind.

idris.name: lfac_2_5_3__flip_pay
idris.note: The payload change the churn rule makes: 0 <-> 1.

idris.name: iret_19_1__assert_fact
idris.note: An entity reassertion with a changed payload retracts the prior fact for the key and asserts a fresh one with a new id, chosen while the old fact is still live so the two ids differ: exactly one live fact per key remains, as the clause requires. The FACT_RETRACT / FACT_ASSERT stream pair is not modelled.

idris.name: lfac_2_5_3__fresh_from
idris.note: Smallest natural not used as a live id and not in the avoid list, by bounded search.

idris.name: lfac_2_5_3__fresh_id
idris.note: A fresh id for the new wrapper, never one bound by the RHS currently running. DS mints monotonically ([IDAT.4.4]) where this reuses the smallest free id; only id equality is ever consulted, so no observable of this model separates the two, and reuse is what lets a looping run return to a literally equal state.

idris.name: iret_19_1__assert
idris.note: A meaningful change is a replace: retract the old fact, insert a fresh wrapper.

idris.name: iret_19_1__assert_unique
idris.note: The replace of a meaningful change keeps one live fact per key: the old fact leaves before the new one enters.

idris.name: iret_19_1__assert_view
idris.note: A replace keeps the view: the retraction of a live fact, then the insertion of a fresh one.

idris.name: lfac_2_5_3__fresh_not_elem
idris.note: The fresh wrapper is not a live fact.

idris.name: iret_19_1__assert_ordered
idris.note: A replace keeps the order: the retraction of a live fact, then the insertion of a fresh one.

idris.name: iret_19_1__assert_sound
idris.note: A replace retracts and inserts: the set is cleared twice.

idris.name: rlow_4_2_1__replace_agree
idris.note: REPLACING AN ENTITY -- the retraction of the old fact then the insertion of the fresh one on the network, one propagation over the result on FireLoop -- keeps the agreement.

idris.name: iret_4_4__ids_identify
idris.note: A replacement is a fresh wrapper with a new id, so within one change an id names one fact.

idris.name: lfac_2_5_3__fresh_from_free
idris.note: The search invariant: with fuel at least the number of excluded values at or above the candidate, the search returns a free value; every excluded candidate passed drops one from that count.

idris.name: lfac_2_5_3__fresh_id_free
idris.note: The replacement's fresh wrapper has an id that is neither live nor bound: among the first |wm| + |avoid| + 1 naturals one qualifies and the search returns the first.
